reason: The Joseph narrative demonstrates the opposite model. Joseph's leadership success is attributed to his faithfulness to God (יְהוָה אִתּוֹ), moral integrity (he refuses Potiphar's wife and justifies his refusal through ethical reasoning), diligence, and wisdom (interpreting dreams). He gains authority through competence and divine favor, not through violence or coercion. Even when facing serious adversity (false accusation, imprisonment), Joseph doesn't resort to violence. His influence over other prisoners and eventually over Pharaoh's officials comes through kindness (שׁרת אתם - he serves them), demonstrated wisdom, and favor with God. The text explicitly contrasts Joseph's peaceful, faithful conduct with his success in leadership roles.
